Description: MNP provides fractional CFO and controller services to small and mid-sized businesses, assigning senior finance leaders on a part-time basis so multiple firms can access executive-level financial strategy and oversight without hiring full-time. This directly implements the fractional executive pool model by deploying experienced CFOs across several clients concurrently, while creating pathways for mid-career finance professionals to build executive experience in diverse industries.
Challenge: Limited Mid-Career Progression and Firm Scale
Solution: Fractional Executive Pool: Organize a cooperative of part-time CFOs, CTOs, CMOs and HR leads available to multiple small businesses so firms can access senior skills at affordable rates while creating pathways for mid-career managers to gain executive experience.
Address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 1200, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

Description: Led by Halifax Partnership, this collaborative brings together major local anchors (HRM, Nova Scotia Health, post-secondary institutions, the Port of Halifax, and others) to align procurement practices that grow local supplier participation and scale SMEs. The group facilitates vendor outreach, joint problem statements, and partnership requirements in bids, fostering capacity-building and R&D collaboration pathways that create higher-skill roles and retain talent.
Challenge: Limited Mid-Career Progression and Firm Scale
Solution: Municipal Procurement for Growth: Advocate for local governments and anchor institutions to structure procurement that favors scaling local SMEs and requires partnerships or capacity-building plans that create senior roles and R&D collaborations.
Address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

Description: Halifax Partnership’s SmartBusiness program is a business retention and expansion (BRE) service that proactively engages established firms to identify growth barriers and connect them to export development, financing, R&D, and market opportunities. Working closely with partners like the Connector Program and post-secondary institutions, it brokers talent matches for hard-to-fill mid-career roles and opens doors to new customers and investors. By helping existing companies scale in-place, the ...
Challenge: Limited Mid-Career Progression and Firm Scale
Solution: Community-Owned Scale-Up Accelerator: Launch a locally governed accelerator focused on scaling existing firms (not just startups) offering business development, market access, talent matching, and investor introductions tailored to mid-career role creation.
Address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

Organization: BioNova (Nova Scotia Life Sciences Industry Association)
Description: BioPort Atlantic, produced by BioNova, hosts the BioInnovation Challenge and investor showcase where life sciences startups pitch to panels of angels and VCs. The event intentionally aggregates regional investors to enable co-investment syndicates and provides standardized pitch materials and feedback that reduce fundraising friction and costs for founders. By curating deal flow and coordinating investor participation, it helps de-risk early checks for individual angels.
Challenge: Entrepreneurship Barriers and Access to Capital
Solution: Local Angel Network and Syndicate: A community-run angel group that aggregates local investors to co-invest in promising startups, runs regular pitch nights, and syndicates investments so individual risk is lower and transaction costs are reduced for entrepreneurs.

Program: Eastlink Wireless Home Internet (Rural Nova Scotia)
Description: Eastlink deploys fixed wireless internet across rural Nova Scotia using a network of towers and rooftop or mast-mounted customer equipment to deliver broadband to clusters of homes where fibre is not yet available. By leveraging tall buildings, existing towers, and new rural sites, the service creates reliable last-mile links that support remote work, learning, and small business operations in underserved communities.
Challenge: Digital Infrastructure Inequities
Solution: Community Mesh and Fixed Wireless Networks: Deploy low-cost mesh or community-managed fixed wireless links (on towers or tall buildings) to connect clusters of homes and businesses where wired fibre is not yet available.

Description: Annapolis Valley Regional Library runs one-on-one technology help and beginner workshops at branches like the Wolfville Memorial Library, covering smartphones, tablets, email, video calls, and cloud-based tools. Sessions emphasize practical digital skills and online safety, helping residents adopt remote work platforms and confidently access government, education, and health services online.
Challenge: Digital Infrastructure Inequities
Solution: Digital Literacy and Support Programs: Offer workshops, drop-in clinics and peer mentoring on digital skills, device setup, cybersecurity and remote work tools at libraries, schools and community centres.

Program: Work in Halifax (Jobs & Labour Market Dashboard)
Description: Halifax Partnership maintains Work in Halifax, a community-facing portal that aggregates real-time local job postings across sectors and links to employer demand, in-demand occupations, and immigration pathways. Through its broader Halifax Index and labour market dashboards, the Partnership publishes up-to-date workforce indicators and skills insights, and promotes training, co-op, and apprenticeship opportunities via partner events so educators and learners can target learning to local demand.
Challenge: Skills Alignment and Work-Integrated Learning Gaps
Solution: Local Labour Market & Skills Dashboard: Maintain a simple community dashboard (managed by municipality or chamber) showing real‑time local openings, skill gaps, apprenticeship opportunities and training calendar so educators and learners can target learning to demand.
Address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

Program: Immigration Employer Support – Inclusive Hiring Resources
Description: Halifax Partnership provides employers with step-by-step resources to recruit and retain diverse talent, including newcomers and international students, through inclusive hiring guides and toolkits. Materials feature sample inclusive job postings, interview and assessment accommodations, bias-reduction checklists, and onboarding best practices tailored for small and medium-sized businesses in the Halifax region.
Challenge: Inclusion, Anti-Racism, and Reconciliation Gaps
Solution: Inclusive Hiring Toolkit for Local Employers: Develop and distribute a practical toolkit with inclusive job posting templates, accessible interview practices, bias-reduction checklists, and onboarding guidance tailored to small and medium local employers.
Address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1103, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

Description: CanadianNanny.ca is an online platform that allows Nova Scotia families to find and share vetted caregivers, explicitly supporting nanny-share arrangements where two or more households split a caregiver’s time and costs. Parents in Halifax, Cape Breton, and rural communities can post nanny-share jobs and filter caregivers by non-standard availability (evenings, weekends, overnights) to cover staggered shifts, then use in-platform messaging to coordinate schedules and logistics.
Challenge: Childcare Availability and Early Learning Workforce
Solution: Shared Nanny and Care Pool: Neighborhood-based shared-nanny arrangements and parent-run scheduling platforms let families share vetted caregivers for staggered hours and non-standard shifts.
Address: 20 Leslie Street, Suite 203, Toronto, ON M4M 3L4

Program: Ward 5 Neighbourhood Centre Early Learning & After School Programs
Description: Ward 5 operates licensed early learning and school-age programs from converted rooms within St. Mark’s Anglican Church in Halifax’s North End, turning underused parish and community hall space into childcare classrooms. The centre’s community board works with the church and local partners to share governance of the space, expanding access to affordable care in a walkable neighbourhood.
Challenge: Childcare Availability and Early Learning Workforce
Solution: Childcare Space Conversion Initiative: Community-led projects to convert underused municipal and commercial spaces—libraries, churches, empty storefronts—into licensed childcare rooms with shared governance.

Description: BayRides provides pre-booked, door-to-door community transportation across the rural St. Margaret’s Bay area and groups riders traveling in similar directions. Dispatchers schedule morning and late-afternoon trips to central hubs in Upper Tantallon and nearby communities, making it practical for parents to reach licensed childcare and after-school programs during peak hours. This demand-responsive, shared-ride model operationalizes coordinated shuttles and ride-shares that bridge rural househ...
Challenge: Childcare Availability and Early Learning Workforce
Solution: Transportation Linkages for Rural Families: Coordinated community shuttles and ride-share arrangements that connect rural families to central childcare hubs during peak hours.
Address: 5284 St. Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H9

Program: Halifax Partnership – Workforce and Policy Collaboration on Child Care
Description: Halifax Partnership convenes employers, post-secondary institutions, and government to collect and analyze local labour market data, identifying child care accessibility as a key constraint on workforce participation. Using these insights, it engages with HRM Planning & Development and council to encourage streamlined zoning/permitting for child care centres and to explore municipal investment mechanisms that help non-profit providers add infant, rural, and non-standard-hours spaces. The Part...
Challenge: Childcare Availability and Early Learning Workforce
Solution: Advocacy and Municipal Support Task Force: A community task force that aggregates local needs data, advocates for zoning, licensing streamlining, municipal subsidies and public investment in childcare.
Address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

Description: SuperNOVA at Dalhousie University delivers mobile, instructor-led STEM programs—including robotics, coding, and engineering design workshops—to communities across Nova Scotia, with a focus on outreach in rural and underserved areas. By bringing equipment and facilitators to local schools and community hubs, SuperNOVA acts as a traveling skills clinic that lowers access barriers and sparks interest in tech and engineering careers.
Challenge: Urban–Rural Opportunity Divide
Solution: Shared maker spaces and mobile skills labs: Develop community maker spaces with tools for woodworking, metalwork, digital fabrication and coding, and run travelling skills clinics that bring hands-on training to remote villages.

Description: The Halifax Seaport Farmers’ Market hosts dozens of Nova Scotia farmers, fishers, food producers, and artisans each weekend on the waterfront, offering a direct marketplace for locally grown and made products. By connecting urban residents and institutional buyers to rural vendors, the market advances buy-local purchasing and helps retain revenue within communities across the province.
Challenge: Urban–Rural Opportunity Divide
Solution: Local procurement and 'buy local' campaigns: Encourage municipal institutions, community organizations and residents to prioritize local suppliers, supporting rural producers, makers and service providers and keeping revenue in the region.

Program: Digital Nova Scotia Hackathons & Policy Design Sprints
Description: Digital Nova Scotia partners with industry and government to run hackathons and problem-solving sprints that engage students, early-career technologists, and civic stakeholders. These events focus on prototyping user-friendly digital tools and service improvements—such as clearer licensing pathways and permit application trackers—to reduce regulatory friction for startups and small businesses.
Challenge: Regulatory Burden and Slow Permitting
Solution: Youth-Led Policy Labs and Hackathons: Host community design sprints where youth, designers, business owners and municipal staff prototype streamlined permitting workflows or digital tools that simplify submission and tracking.
Address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

Description: Open Arms’ Housing Support Program engages landlords across the Annapolis Valley to secure and sustain housing for people at risk of homelessness, mediating tenancy issues and arranging practical supports. The team provides rapid-response outreach, tenancy coaching, and access to emergency funds for rent/utility arrears or damage deposits to prevent evictions and keep people stably housed.
Challenge: Public Safety, Housing Insecurity, and Substance Use Harms
Solution: Supportive tenancy and landlord mediation program: Create a community mediation hub to work with landlords and tenants, offering incentives, damage mitigation funds, tenancy coaching and rapid-response support to keep people housed.

Organization: Recreation Nova Scotia (with South Shore regional partners)
Description: South Shore Connect is a community-driven directory for programs, supports, and active living opportunities across Lunenburg, Queens, and Shelburne counties. Local organizations and residents submit program listings that are reviewed by regional partners, ensuring up-to-date, non-duplicative information that families can search by location and interest. Listings are print-friendly and are used by partners to create seasonal or topic-specific booklets for offline use.
Challenge: Fragmented Governance and Data Silos
Solution: Community Services Directory (crowd-sourced): Build and maintain a simple, searchable, crowd-sourced directory of local programs, supports and contact points (accessible online and as a printable booklet). Community organizations, libraries, schools and residents contribute updates, keeping information current and reducing duplication for youth and families navigating services.
Address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, Suite 407, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

Program: Maritime SPOR SUPPORT Unit (MSSU) – Nova Scotia Site
Organization: IWK Health Centre (in partnership with Dalhousie University and Nova Scotia Health)
Description: MSSU brings together health system decision-makers, clinicians, community organizations, patients, and academic partners to co-design and use de-identified, aggregated data for patient-oriented research and planning across Nova Scotia (and the Maritimes). Governed data access committees, privacy reviews, and standardized data-use agreements define how partners contribute to and use shared datasets while protecting confidentiality. This collaborative governance reduces fragmentation and enable...
Challenge: Fragmented Governance and Data Silos
Solution: Community Data Cooperative (data trust): Form a voluntary cooperative of local nonprofits, schools and municipal partners to share aggregated, anonymized service-use data. The cooperative sets rules for access and use, enabling joint planning while keeping control in community hands and protecting privacy.

Program: Maritime SPOR SUPPORT Unit – Nova Scotia Site
Description: The MSSU (NS) supports cross-organization, patient-oriented projects by providing privacy-by-design expertise, standardized data-sharing/transfer agreement templates, and plain-language consent templates that enable limited, purpose-specific information exchange. Its guidance includes de-identification methods and retention/archiving clauses so health and community partners can coordinate services and evaluate outcomes while protecting youth and family privacy.
Challenge: Fragmented Governance and Data Silos
Solution: Community Privacy & Data-Sharing Agreement Template: Develop an easy-to-use template agreement and privacy guidelines that local organizations can sign to enable safe, limited data sharing for coordination. Include plain-language consent scripts for youth and families, and practical clauses about anonymization and retention.
Address: Centre for Clinical Research, 5790 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 1V7

Description: Halifax Partnership maintains a comprehensive digital relocation portal that aggregates job opportunities, neighbourhood and housing information, childcare and newcomer services, community events, and newcomer success stories. A local team curates and updates content and tools (including job links and settlement resources) and promotes the portal through employer networks and alumni/diaspora outreach to help prospective and returning residents make informed decisions.
Challenge: Provincial Brand and Talent Attraction Narrative
Solution: Local Digital Relocation Portal: Create and maintain a simple, community-run web portal with practical relocation information (jobs, housing listings, childcare, service contacts, events, testimonials). Keep content updated by a rotating local editorial team and promote it to alumni networks.
Address: 5151 George Street, Suite 1277, Halifax, NS B3J 1M5

Program: Work in Halifax Talent Attraction Toolkit
Description: Halifax Partnership provides employers with ready-to-use talent attraction assets—messaging, images, videos, and market insights—that can be dropped into job postings, career pages, and social media to sell the lifestyle and opportunities of living and working in Halifax. The team hosts employer info sessions and webinars that coach small businesses on writing compelling postings and using short recruitment videos and social content to showcase workplace culture, benefits, and career pathways.
Challenge: Provincial Brand and Talent Attraction Narrative
Solution: Employer Branding Toolkit for Small Businesses: Develop an easy toolkit and templates local businesses can use to communicate workplace culture, benefits, career pathways, and remote-friendly roles. Host workshops to help employers produce job postings and short recruitment videos that sell living and working locally.
Address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

Description: NSCC’s accelerated CCA certificate delivers fast-tracked classroom learning combined with guaranteed clinical placements in long-term care and home care organizations across Nova Scotia. Developed with employers and Nova Scotia Health, the program embeds mentorship and work-integrated learning so graduates can move quickly into in-demand support roles and, if desired, bridge onward into LPN/RN or other allied health pathways within their communities.
Challenge: Skills Alignment and Work-Integrated Learning Gaps
Solution: Community Health & Care Training Pipeline: Partner local clinics, long‑term care facilities and colleges to create guaranteed practicum placements, fast‑track certificates for support roles, and mentorship pathways into nursing and allied health within the community.

Program: IGNITE Atlantic Rural Pop‑up Skills Labs
Description: IGNITE Atlantic runs pop‑up skills labs and mobile workshops that bring hands‑on digital skills, prototyping, and entrepreneurship training to rural communities in Western and Northern Nova Scotia. Sessions are set up in community venues and employer worksites, often co‑designed with local companies that mentor participants and host hiring mixers or project showcases to connect graduates to interviews. The approach lowers access barriers and rapidly aligns short, practical training with immed...
Challenge: Skills Alignment and Work-Integrated Learning Gaps
Solution: Mobile Training Units & Pop‑up Skills Labs: Deploy mobile training trailers or pop‑up labs that bring short technical and trade training to rural communities (e.g., welding, carpentry basics, digital skills), coordinated with local employers who pledge interviews for graduates.

Program: IGNITE Atlantic – Business Workshops (Digital Storytelling & Recruitment Marketing)
Description: IGNITE Atlantic runs frequent workshops that teach small businesses how to write effective, inclusive job postings and produce short, mobile-friendly recruitment videos and social content. Sessions emphasize showcasing workplace culture, flexibility (including remote-friendly roles), and the advantages of living and working in rural Nova Scotia, with staff providing light-touch coaching and templates so employers leave with ready-to-use materials.
Challenge: Provincial Brand and Talent Attraction Narrative
Solution: Employer Branding Toolkit for Small Businesses: Develop an easy toolkit and templates local businesses can use to communicate workplace culture, benefits, career pathways, and remote-friendly roles. Host workshops to help employers produce job postings and short recruitment videos that sell living and working locally.
Address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3R7

Description: CANS Emerging Leaders is a peer network for early- and mid-career construction professionals that hosts regular meetups, site tours, skills workshops, and mentoring events. By connecting tradespeople and project staff with employers and peers, the group creates referral channels and practical skill-sharing that help workers demonstrate competencies and secure roles while awaiting interprovincial trade certification or local credential recognition.
Challenge: Credential Recognition and Labour Mobility Frictions
Solution: Peer Professional Networks and Industry Circles: Sector-specific community networks (health, trades, tech, arts) that host regular peer review sessions, skills-sharing workshops and referral groups to help candidates demonstrate competencies and find local opportunities while awaiting formal recognition.
Address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

Description: CANS convenes contractors, developers, and suppliers to identify bottlenecks in municipal planning, permitting, and inspection processes across Nova Scotia. The association aggregates member feedback into policy briefs and presentations to municipal councils and staff, advocating for standardized checklists, fixed review timelines, transparent fees, and simplified local rules that cut red tape and accelerate construction and housing delivery.
Challenge: Regulatory Burden and Slow Permitting
Solution: Regulatory Feedback and Red‑Tape Reduction Campaigns: Coordinate structured community feedback to municipal councils identifying the most burdensome rules and proposing simpler, local solutions (e.g., fee waivers, timeline caps).

Program: HRM Living Wage Requirement for Service Contracts
Description: Halifax Regional Municipality has adopted a living wage requirement for many externally contracted services, embedding living wage standards into municipal procurement to ensure contracted workers are paid at or above the local living wage. The municipality informs vendors and community partners about the policy and its phased implementation, using procurement guidelines and education to encourage wider employer adoption and lift overall wage floors across the region.
Challenge: Wage and Career Competitiveness
Solution: Local Living Wage Campaign: Community-led advocacy to encourage municipalities, local institutions and larger employers to adopt a living wage policy; includes public education, employer toolkits, and phased implementation plans to raise average wages.

Program: Task Force on the Commemoration of Edward Cornwallis and the Recognition and Commemoration of Indigenous History (Implementation)
Description: Halifax Regional Municipality established a joint task force with Mi'kmaq leaders and knowledge keepers to co-develop concrete recommendations for how the city should address monuments, place names, and the public recognition of Mi’kmaq history. HRM is implementing these actions through an ongoing reconciliation process that includes renaming streets, updating protocols and signage, and advancing cultural education, with progress reported publicly to Council and the community.
Challenge: Inclusion, Anti-Racism, and Reconciliation Gaps
Solution: Community-led Reconciliation Action Plans: Form a local reconciliation working group with Mi'kmaq Elders, leaders, and youth to co-develop short- and long-term community actions (land stewardship, cultural education, monuments, protocols) with measurable timelines and annual public reporting.

Program: HalifACT – Coastal Hazard Setbacks and Adaptation Planning
Description: HalifACT is Halifax Regional Municipality’s climate action plan, which embeds coastal hazard mapping, sea-level rise allowances, and shoreline setback requirements into the Regional Plan and land-use by-laws. Through public engagement sessions and community planning processes, HRM works with residents and developers to direct new development away from high-erosion and flood-risk shorelines and to consider voluntary retreat of vulnerable structures over time. This implements local shoreline se...
Challenge: Climate Resilience and Environmental Risks
Solution: Local Shoreline Setback and Managed Retreat Planning: Facilitate community conversations and small-scale pilot buyouts or voluntary relocation incentives, guided by local priorities, to reduce long-term risk in high-erosion zones.

Program: Downtown Halifax Bonus Zoning Public Benefit Program (HRM by Design)
Description: Halifax’s downtown planning framework uses negotiated development agreements and density bonusing to secure public benefits from private projects. Eligible public benefits include on-site cultural/community uses and public art, allowing the municipality to require developers to deliver dedicated cultural space (e.g., studios, rehearsal or small performance space) in new buildings or to provide cash-in-lieu contributions to municipal public benefit reserves (including the Public Art Reserve) w...
Challenge: Arts, Culture, and Nightlife Space Constraints
Solution: Partnerships with Developers for Cultural Floors: Negotiate community-benefit agreements with residential and commercial developers to include dedicated affordable cultural spaces (studios, micro-theatres) or in-lieu contributions to a municipal arts space fund.

Description: Halifax Regional Municipality runs a single, one-stop application for festivals and events that coordinates all required municipal permits and reviews through one intake. Staff from parks, right-of-way/traffic, planning (site permissions), building (tents/stages), fire, and police review files together and liaise with Nova Scotia Public Health for food vendor requirements, issuing coordinated decisions within published timelines. This co-located, cross-department workflow functions as a pract...
Challenge: Regulatory Burden and Slow Permitting
Solution: One-Stop Permit Pilot Partnership: Partner with the municipality to run a time-limited one-stop shop pilot that co-locates staff from planning, building, business licensing and health to issue combined decisions within set timelines.

Program: Healthcare Career Pathways for Newcomers (including IEN Bridging)
Organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
Description: ISANS supports internationally educated nurses and other internationally trained health professionals with career advising, exam preparation, mentorship, and employer connections, often in collaboration with Nova Scotia Health and long-term care agencies. The program helps participants secure supervised work experiences or observerships and guided practicum pathways, accelerating their integration into nursing and allied health roles that address local workforce needs.
Challenge: Skills Alignment and Work-Integrated Learning Gaps
Solution: Community Health & Care Training Pipeline: Partner local clinics, long‑term care facilities and colleges to create guaranteed practicum placements, fast‑track certificates for support roles, and mentorship pathways into nursing and allied health within the community.
Address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

Program: Welcoming Workplaces: Equity, Diversity & Inclusion Training
Organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
Description: ISANS’ Welcoming Workplaces offers anti-racism, anti-oppression, and human rights training and policy reviews for businesses and community groups. They work with employers to draft and implement anti-harassment and anti-discrimination policies, establish reporting and complaint processes, and connect newcomers who experience hate incidents with legal and support services.
Challenge: Inclusion, Anti-Racism, and Reconciliation Gaps
Solution: Community Safety and Anti-Harassment Protocols: Work with community groups and businesses to adopt clear anti-harassment policies, reporting mechanisms, and rapid-response supports for incidents targeting race, Indigeneity, gender identity, or disability.
Address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

Program: Indigenous Cultural Safety and KAIROS Blanket Exercise
Description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre facilitates Mi’kmaw cultural safety training, including the KAIROS Blanket Exercise and workshops on land acknowledgements, reconciliation, and working respectfully with urban Indigenous communities. Sessions are led by Elders, Knowledge Keepers, and experienced facilitators, and are offered regularly to employers, educators, and first responders, with options to tailor and subsidize delivery through partnerships.
Challenge: Inclusion, Anti-Racism, and Reconciliation Gaps
Solution: Local Anti-Racism and Inclusion Training: Offer regular, subsidized anti-racism, cultural safety, and accessibility trainings co-designed and delivered by community representatives and subject experts for employers, educators, first responders, and service providers.

Program: Wije’winen Project – Community Engagement & Youth Programming
Description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Wije’winen initiative conducts ongoing community engagement circles and co-design workshops with Mi’kmaq youth, Elders, and urban Indigenous community members to shape an integrated hub of services (including housing navigation, employment supports, and cultural programming). These sessions elevate youth leadership and ensure programs are co-created with and for Indigenous youth, while also inviting collaboration with non-Indigenous partners to improve s...
Challenge: Youth Voice and Civic Engagement Deficit
Solution: Community Co-design Workshops: Host regular co-design sessions where youth and community stakeholders jointly develop programs and services (housing, transit, employment supports), using facilitation that centers youth voices, including rural and Mi'kmaq youth.

Description: The HRCE Superintendent’s Student Advisory Council convenes secondary students from across the region to advise education leaders on system navigation and student supports. Youth review how school, public health, mental health, and community services intersect, help test information portals and referral processes, and recommend clearer pathways for accessing help. Their insights inform cross-agency collaboration and responsible information-sharing, advancing coordinated, youth-centered servic...
Challenge: Fragmented Governance and Data Silos
Solution: Youth Advisory Council on Service Integration: Create a council of young people from diverse backgrounds to review how services are organized, test navigation tools, advise on data-sharing practices and champion solutions. Their lived experience ensures community efforts stay youth-centered and practical.
Address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

Description: Switch temporarily opens streets to people and closes them to car traffic, creating safe, pop‑up walking and cycling routes that demonstrate how active transportation can work for everyday trips. The Ecology Action Centre coordinates volunteers, local councils, and businesses to deliver these events and often helps communities parlay successful pilots into small grants and permanent infrastructure improvements. The program also advances policies and practices—such as winter maintenance priori...
Challenge: Transportation and Regional Connectivity Gaps
Solution: Active Transportation Campaigns and Infrastructure Projects: Mobilize volunteers and local councils to build and maintain safe walking and cycling paths (including snow clearance), host bike-to-work days, and secure small grants for infrastructure that shortens local trips.

Program: Ecology Action Centre – Coastal Restoration (Living Shorelines, Dunes, and Salt Marsh)
Description: The Ecology Action Centre coordinates community-based coastal restoration, including native dune grass plantings, living shoreline pilots with partners, and support for salt marsh conservation and restoration. By using natural features like coir logs, brush bundles, and native vegetation, EAC projects aim to reduce wave energy, encourage sediment capture, and protect public access and coastal infrastructure. Workshops and volunteer events engage youth and residents in hands-on stewardship and...
Challenge: Climate Resilience and Environmental Risks
Solution: Living Shoreline and Saltmarsh Restoration: Community volunteers, local NGOs, and municipalities collaborate to restore dunes, saltmarshes, eelgrass beds, and oyster reefs to reduce wave energy, trap sediments, and slow coastal erosion while enhancing habitat.

Program: Coastal Cleanup and Marine Debris Action
Description: Ecology Action Centre engages volunteers in coastal and harbour shoreline cleanups across Nova Scotia, often in partnership with community groups and schools. By removing driftwood accumulations, plastic waste, and derelict gear from beaches and riparian zones, these cleanups help reduce erosion impacts, protect marine and coastal biodiversity, and lower wildfire risk in dry seasons.
Challenge: Climate Resilience and Environmental Risks
Solution: Volunteer Beach and Riparian Debris Removal: Regular community cleanups to remove driftwood, abandoned materials, and invasive debris that can worsen erosion, damage habitats, or increase fire risk when dry.

Program: Coastal Adaptation: Community Outreach on Sea-Level Rise & Storm Surges
Description: Ecology Action Centre works with coastal communities to communicate flood and storm-surge risks and to promote preparedness and resilient practices for homes and infrastructure. Through workshops, guides, and local engagement, they translate risk maps and climate projections into practical steps residents can take, including knowing high-risk zones, planning evacuation routes, and protecting property.
Challenge: Climate Resilience and Environmental Risks
Solution: Public Education and Risk Communication Campaigns: Ongoing outreach in multiple languages about flood zones, evacuation routes, insurance options, and practical household preparedness steps to increase readiness across communities.

Description: The Ecology Action Centre hosts paid internships and co-op placements that embed youth in policy, planning, and program design across climate, transportation, coastal, and environmental justice initiatives. Interns co-develop community programs, contribute to policy submissions and planning processes, and support engagement with municipalities and provincial agencies—giving youth meaningful roles in shaping public-interest outcomes.
Challenge: Youth Voice and Civic Engagement Deficit
Solution: Youth Civic Apprenticeships: Create short-term paid apprenticeships in local government, NGOs, and community organizations that place youth in policy, planning, and program-design roles to build skills and institutional knowledge.

Program: Halifax Waterfront Development Agreements for Cultural Public Realm
Description: Build Nova Scotia negotiates ground leases and development agreements with private developers on the Halifax waterfront that require publicly accessible cultural spaces and year‑round programming. Agreements secure cultural floors in mixed-use projects (e.g., event plazas, gallery and exhibition areas, performance locations) or require financial contributions that help program and maintain cultural public spaces—linking private development to affordable, publicly available arts venues.
Challenge: Arts, Culture, and Nightlife Space Constraints
Solution: Partnerships with Developers for Cultural Floors: Negotiate community-benefit agreements with residential and commercial developers to include dedicated affordable cultural spaces (studios, micro-theatres) or in-lieu contributions to a municipal arts space fund.
Address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

Description: Volta hosts recurring peer roundtables and community events that bring together founders and senior leaders of small technology firms to discuss growth tactics, hiring challenges, and market expansion. These forums create a trusted space for leaders to exchange playbooks, make referrals, and identify partnership opportunities, which can translate into collaborative go-to-market efforts and larger joint pursuits.
Challenge: Limited Mid-Career Progression and Firm Scale
Solution: Local Scale-Up Peer Network: Create a community-run network where leaders of small firms meet regularly to share growth strategies, talent challenges, and partnership opportunities, enabling informal benchmarking, referrals, and joint bids that increase firm scale.

Description: Volta convenes recurring peer-to-peer founder circles and facilitated discussions where startup leaders share practical solutions on hiring, scaling, and leadership, while receiving coaching from experienced mentors and peers. These small-group sessions operate as mentorship circles that deepen networks and improve mid-career satisfaction for tech professionals choosing to build their careers in Nova Scotia.
Challenge: Limited Mid-Career Progression and Firm Scale
Solution: Peer Mentorship Circles: Set up facilitated peer groups of mid-career professionals across sectors to exchange problem-solving, career planning, and leadership coaching, increasing retention by improving career satisfaction and networks.
Address: Suite 100, 1505 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

Description: Volta Academy delivers recurring cohorts and workshops that train founders to craft investor-ready pitches, develop financial models, and understand governance best practices. Its Mentor Network and Office Hours connect startups with volunteer entrepreneurs, investors, and service providers for ongoing coaching and feedback, directly increasing their readiness to attract capital.
Challenge: Entrepreneurship Barriers and Access to Capital
Solution: Investor-Readiness Bootcamps and Mentor Network: Volunteer entrepreneurs, investors and service providers run regular bootcamps and a mentorship registry to help founders craft investor-ready pitches, financial models and governance structures, increasing their ability to attract capital.

Program: Volta Funding Panel & Office Hours Series
Description: Volta regularly convenes funding panels and lender office hours that bring together BDC, credit unions, commercial banks, and startup founders to discuss real financing cases and underwriting expectations. These facilitated sessions let lenders explain risk frameworks while founders share traction data and collateral challenges, leading to practical checklists, feedback loops on lending criteria, and pilots such as revenue-based or milestone-tied credit options tailored to early-stage companies.
Challenge: Entrepreneurship Barriers and Access to Capital
Solution: Lender–Startup Dialogue Workshops: Facilitated workshops where local lenders, credit unions and startups exchange perspectives, share case studies, and co-develop pragmatic lending criteria and pilot products that balance risk management with startup realities.
Address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

Description: Volta’s hiring and talent events connect high-growth startups and tech employers with students, grads, and professionals through showcase booths, company pitches, and networking.
